questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered a user interface component?

options.text: The border of a text input field.

questions.explanation: Borders, icons, and buttons are graphical components that need a clear boundary so interactions can be identified.
questions.hint: Think about the parts of a form that are actually clicked.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Identify what qualifies as a user interface component.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum contrast ratio for non-text components like icons and borders?
questions.explanation: The research gives graphical objects and user interface states a threshold of 3 against adjacent colors.
questions.hint: It is the lower of the two standard thresholds.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Understand the 3 ratio requirement for borders and icons.

questions.prompt: How can adjacent slices in a pie chart be made distinguishable?

options.text: Ensure the slices have contrast of at least 3, or add dark borders between them.
Make all the slices the exact same color.
Remove all labels and legends from the chart.
Ensure the slices have a contrast ratio of 1 to 1.

questions.explanation: If adjacent colors do not meet the stated ratio, they can blend together. A dark border can provide a boundary.
questions.hint: Consider how to physically separate two similar colors touching each other.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Apply contrast rules to data visualizations and charts.
